Interviewer: To start, I would like to begin with a big question: tell me the story of your life. Start from the beginning -- from your childhood, to education, to family and relationships, and to any major life events you may have had.

Agent: I was born and raised in a small town in Colorado. My childhood was filled with outdoor adventures and tight-knit community connections. I grew up with my parents and two younger sisters, and our family was very supportive and close. After high school, I attended Colorado State University, where I majored in environmental science. It was there that I met my life partner, Sam. We traveled a lot together after college, exploring national parks and developing a strong love for nature. A few years post-graduation, I started working for a non-profit organization focusing on conservation efforts, which has been my passion ever since. We recently welcomed our first child, a beautiful baby girl named Lily, which is definitely the most important event in my life so far.

Interviewer: To start, I would like to begin with a big question: tell me the story of your life. Start from the beginning -- from your childhood, to education, to family and relationships, and to any major life events you may have had.

Agent: I was born and raised in a small town in the Midwest. My childhood was filled with outdoor adventures and playing sports with the neighborhood kids. I attended a local high school where I developed a keen interest in science. My passion led me to pursue a degree in biology at a nearby university. I've always valued education and have continued to take courses throughout my life. In terms of family, I'm very close to my parents and have one younger sister with whom I share many childhood memories. I've had a few significant relationships over the years but have not yet settled down with a long-term partner. One major life event was when I decided to move to the East Coast for my career, which opened up many new opportunities for me.

Interviewer: Moving to present time, tell me more about family who are important to you. Do you have a partner, or children?

Agent: Currently, I am single and do not have children. However, I am very close to my sister who lives nearby, and we see each other frequently.

Interviewer: Tell me about anyone else in your life we haven't discussed (like friends or romantic partners). Are there people outside of your family who are important to you?

Agent: Outside of my family, I have a close-knit group of friends from college, and we make it a point to meet at least once a year. My lifelong friend, Jenna, is like a sibling to me, and we often catch up for hiking trips whenever possible. Also, I am part of a community gardening club where I've formed lasting friendships based on mutual interests.

Interviewer: Tell me about anyone else in your life we haven't discussed (like friends or romantic partners). Are there people outside of your family who are important to you?

Agent: I have a small but close-knit group of friends whom I consider my extended family. We’ve supported each other through thick and thin over the years, and I cherish the deep friendships we've built.

Interviewer: Now let's talk about your current neighborhood. Tell me all about the neighborhood and area in which you are living now.

Agent: I live in a vibrant, diverse neighborhood in the city. It's bustling with energy and has a rich cultural scene. There are plenty of parks and cafes, and I love the community events that bring people together.

Interviewer: Living any place has its ups and downs. Tell me about what it's been like for you living here.

Agent: Living here has been a wonderful experience for me. I enjoy the cultural diversity and the endless opportunities to learn and engage with different communities. However, like any city, it has its downsides, such as the noise and occasional traffic hassle. Nonetheless, the positives far outweigh the negatives for me.

Interviewer: Tell me about the people who live with you right now, even people who are staying here temporarily.

Agent: I live with my partner and our two kids. My partner works from home, and the kids are in school during weekdays.

Interviewer: Is there anyone who usually lives here but is away - traveling, at school, or in a hospital?

Agent: No, there is no one who usually lives here but is currently away.

Interviewer: Is anyone in your household a temporary member, or is everyone a permanent member of the household?

Agent: Everyone in my household is a permanent member.

Interviewer: Some people say they vote in every election, some tell us they don't vote at all. How about you?

Agent: I try to vote in every election, as I believe it's a crucial part of participating in democracy.

Interviewer: Is there anyone who usually lives here but is away - traveling, at school, or in a hospital?

Agent: No, everyone who usually lives here is present.

Interviewer: If you have children, tell me about a typical weekday during the school year for your children. What is their daily routine? And what are after school activities your children participate in?

Agent: I don't have children, so there is no school year routine in my household.

Interviewer: At what kind of job or jobs do you work, and when do you work?

Agent: I work full-time as a software engineer at a tech company. My work hours are 9 AM to 5 PM, Monday through Friday.

Interviewer: How have you been thinking about race in the U.S. recently?

Agent: I've been thinking about the history of race relations in the U.S. and the importance of continuing education and dialogue to tackle racism effectively.

Interviewer: What other experiences with law enforcement stand out in your mind?

Agent: I remember being pulled over for a minor traffic violation, and the officer was quite respectful and courteous. It stood out because I've heard mixed stories, but my personal experience was positive.

Interviewer: Some people tell us about experiences of arrest - of loved ones, family members, friends, or themselves. How about for you?

Agent: I haven't had experiences of arrest personally or with any close family members, though I've had friends who have been arrested for minor infractions.

Interviewer: How have you been thinking about race in the U.S. recently?

Agent: I've been thinking about the history of race relations in the U.S. and the importance of continuing education and dialogue to tackle racism effectively.

Interviewer: How have you been thinking about the issues Black Lives Matter raises?

Agent: I've been trying to educate myself more about the history and the current racial disparities in the U.S. justice system.

Interviewer: How have you responded to the increased focus on race and/or racism and policing? Some people tell us they're aware of the issue but keep their thoughts to themselves, others say they've talked to family and friends, others have joined protests. What about you?

Agent: I've had discussions with friends and family about these issues, trying to understand different perspectives and raise awareness.

Interviewer: How have you responded to the increased focus on race and/or racism and policing? Some people tell us they're aware of the issue but keep their thoughts to themselves, others say they've talked to family and friends, others have joined protests. What about you?

Agent: I've had discussions with friends and family about these issues, trying to understand different perspectives and raise awareness.

Interviewer: Sometimes, health problems get in the way. They can even affect people's ability to work or care for their children. How about you?

Agent: Thankfully, my health has not gotten in the way of my work or personal responsibilities. I feel fortunate to be able to maintain a good balance.

Interviewer: What about people you're close to? How have they responded to the increased focus on race and/or racism and policing?

Agent: People I'm close to have generally been proactive; many have attended local protests or participated in community discussions.

Interviewer: Sometimes, it's not your health problem, but the health of a loved one. Has this been an issue for you?

Agent: I'm relieved — none of my loved ones have had any major health issues recently. How about you? Is everyone well on your side?

Interviewer: Tell me about anything big that has happened in the past two years related to your health: any medical diagnoses, flare-ups of chronic conditions, broken bones, pain - anything like that.

Agent: In the past two years, I've been fortunate to not have any major health issues. I did have a minor sprain in my ankle that took a few weeks to heal, but nothing more serious.

Interviewer: Now we're going to talk a bit more about what life was like for you over the past year. Tell me all about how you have been feeling.

Agent: Over the past year, I've had a mixture of emotions. I've experienced stress due to changes in my routine but also found joy in small things and personal growth.

Interviewer: Have you or your immediate family ever used alternative forms of medicine? This might include indigenous, non-western, or informal forms of care.

Agent: Yes, occasionally we've used herbal remedies passed down through generations for mild conditions and they seem to work well for us.

Interviewer: Sometimes, it's not your health problem, but the health of a loved one. Has this been an issue for you?

Agent: Thankfully, I have not had to deal with any major health issues in my family. We are all relatively healthy and support each other in maintaining our well-being.

Interviewer: Have you or your immediate family ever used alternative forms of medicine? This might include indigenous, non-western, or informal forms of care.

Agent: I haven't extensively used alternative medicine, but I have tried herbal teas for relaxation and chamomile for better sleep.

Interviewer: How are you and your family coping with, or paying for, your health care needs right now?

Agent: We have a stable income and good health insurance, which helps us manage our healthcare expenses effectively.

Interviewer: Now we're going to talk a bit more about what life was like for you over the past year. Tell me all about how you have been feeling.

Agent: Over the past year, I've had a mixture of emotions. I've experienced stress due to changes in my routine but also found joy in small things and personal growth.

Interviewer: Some people say they struggle with depression, anxiety, or something else like that. How about for you?

Agent: I occasionally experience anxiety, particularly during stressful situations, but I manage it with mindfulness techniques and exercise.

Interviewer: Now we're going to talk a bit more about what life was like for you over the past year. Tell me all about how you have been feeling.

Agent: Over the past year, I've felt a mix of anxiety due to uncertainties, but also gratitude for the time spent with family and the support of friends.

Interviewer: Tell me a story about a time in the last year when you were in a rough place or struggling emotionally.

Agent: There was a time last year when I felt overwhelmed by isolation during the lockdowns, but reaching out to friends and talking about it helped me cope.

Interviewer: Some people tell us they use Facebook, Instagram, or other social media to stay connected with the wider world. How about you? Tell me all about how you use these types of platforms.

Agent: I use platforms like Instagram and LinkedIn to stay updated, follow interesting content, and maintain professional connections.

Interviewer: Some people say they struggle with depression, anxiety, or something else like that. How about for you?

Agent: I occasionally experience anxiety, particularly during stressful situations, but I manage it with mindfulness techniques and exercise.

Interviewer: Some people say they use Facebook or Twitter to get (emotional or financial) support during tough times. What about you?

Agent: I tend to seek emotional support from close friends and family rather than social media, although I occasionally read supportive posts online.

Interviewer: Tell me about any recent changes in your level of stress, worry, and your emotional coping strategies.

Agent: Recently, I've felt an increase in stress but have been trying to cope by practicing meditation and setting aside time for hobbies.

Interviewer: How much did your household spend in the past month? Is that the usual amount? And if not, how much do you usually spend and on what?

Agent: Our household spent about $3,000 last month, which is fairly typical. We usually spend the most on rent, groceries, utilities, and transportation.

Interviewer: Any lodgers, boarders, or employees who live here?

Agent: No, we don't have any lodgers, boarders, or employees living with us.

Interviewer: Who shares the responsibility for the rent, mortgage, or other household expenses?

Agent: My partner and I share the responsibility for the rent and household expenses.

Interviewer: Overall, how do you feel about your financial situation?

Agent: Overall, I feel cautiously optimistic about my financial situation. While I'm not wealthy, I have a steady income and a plan for managing expenses and savings.

Interviewer: Now we'd like to talk about how you make ends meet and what the monthly budget looks like for you and your family. What were your biggest expenses last month?

Agent: Last month, our biggest expenses were the mortgage payment, utilities, groceries, and the back-to-school supplies for the kids.

Interviewer: In the past year, how many weeks did you work (for a few hours, including paid vacation, paid sick leave, and military service)?

Agent: I worked 48 weeks in the past year, including my vacation time.

Interviewer: Some people have student loans or credit card debt. Others take out loans from family or friends or find other ways of borrowing money. Tell me about all the debts you're paying on right now.

Agent: I am currently paying off a student loan and have a small balance on my credit card that I'm managing.

Interviewer: Tell me all about how you coped with any extra expenses in the past months.

Agent: To cope with extra expenses, we've been tightening our budget by cutting down on non-essential spending and sometimes dipping into our savings when necessary.

Interviewer: Now, in the past month, how many jobs did you work, including part time, evening, or weekend work?

Agent: I worked two jobs in the past month, including one part-time and one weekend job.

Interviewer: Are you now married, widowed, divorced, separated, or have you never been married? If you are not currently married, are you currently living with a romantic partner?

Agent: I have never been married, but I am currently living with my romantic partner.

Interviewer: What is or was your occupation? In this occupation, what kind of work do you do and what are the most important activities or duties?

Agent: I am a graphic designer. My work primarily involves creating visual concepts and designs for digital and print media.

Interviewer: In total, how much did your household make in the past month?

Agent: Our household made $4,500.

Interviewer: Some people save for big things, like a home, while others save for a rainy day. How about for you (in the last year)?

Agent: I save both for big things like a home and also set aside some money for a rainy day.

Interviewer: Are you enrolled in school?

Agent: No, I am not currently enrolled in school.

Interviewer: What is or was your occupation? In this occupation, what kind of work do you do and what are the most important activities or duties?

Agent: I work as a software developer, focusing on creating and maintaining web applications. My most important duties include coding, testing, and collaborating with a team.

Interviewer: In the past week, did you work for pay (even for 1 hour) at a job or business?

Agent: Yes, I did work for pay in the past week.

Interviewer: Tell me more about your workplace. How long have you been at your current job? How would you describe the benefits that come with your job? (This could include things like health benefits, paid time off, vacation, and sick time.)

Agent: I've been at my current job for 2 years. The benefits are decent, including health insurance, paid time off, and vacation days.

Interviewer: Switching gears a bit, let's talk a little about tax time. Did you file taxes last year (the most recent year)?

Agent: Yes, I did file taxes last year.

Interviewer: How often do you get paid?

Agent: I get paid bi-weekly.

Interviewer: Tell me more about your workplace. How long have you been at your current job? How would you describe the benefits that come with your job? (This could include things like health benefits, paid time off, vacation, and sick time.)

Agent: I've been at my current job for 2 years. The benefits include health insurance and paid time off.

Interviewer: Tell me about how predictable your work schedule is. How would you describe your job in terms of flexibility with your hours?

Agent: My work schedule is somewhat predictable, but there is some flexibility in adjusting hours if needed.

Interviewer: Some people say it's hard to take or keep a job because of child care. How about for you?

Agent: Child care isn't an issue for me, so it's not hard to take or keep my job.

Interviewer: What would it be like for you if you had to spend $400 for an emergency? Would you have the money, and if not, how would you get it?

Agent: If faced with a $400 emergency, I would likely need to dip into my savings to cover the cost. Fortunately, I've been diligent about having an emergency fund, so I would have the money available.

Interviewer: Tell me about times over the last year when your income was especially low. And tell me about all the things you did to make ends meet during that time.

Agent: Last year, my income was especially low during the summer months due to reduced freelance opportunities. To make ends meet, I took a part-time job at a local bookstore, cut down on non-essential expenses, and utilized a small emergency fund to cover necessary bills.

Interviewer: Were you born in the United States? If you were not born in the U.S., what country were you born, and what year did you first come to the U.S. to live?

Agent: Yes, I was born in the United States.

Interviewer: Overall, how do you feel about your financial situation?

Agent: Overall, I feel cautiously optimistic about my financial situation. While I'm not wealthy, I have a steady income and a plan for managing expenses and savings.

Interviewer: What is the highest degree or grade you've completed?

Agent: The highest degree I have completed is a Bachelor's degree.

Interviewer: For our records, we also need your date of birth. Could you please provide that?

Agent: May 15, 1990

Interviewer: What race or races do you identify with?

Agent: I identify as White.

Interviewer: Have you been enrolled in school during the past 3 months?

Agent: No, I have not been enrolled in school during the past 3 months.

Interviewer: Are you of Hispanic, Latinx, or Spanish origin?

Agent: No, I am not of Hispanic, Latinx, or Spanish origin.

Interviewer: What race or races do you identify with?

Agent: I identify as White.

Interviewer: Have you been enrolled in school during the past 3 months?

Agent: No, I have not been enrolled in school during the past 3 months.

Interviewer: Did you live with both your own mother and father when you were 16?

Agent: Yes, I lived with both my own mother and father when I was 16.

Interviewer: Have you ever served on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces, Reserves, or National Guard?

Agent: No, I have never served on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces, Reserves, or National Guard.

Interviewer: Who else did you live with?

Agent: I also lived with my younger brother.

Interviewer: What religion do you identify with, if any?

Agent: I identify as agnostic.

Interviewer: What kind of place did he work for? What kind of business was it? What did they make or do where he worked?

Agent: He worked for a construction company that specialized in electrical contracting. They focused on building and infrastructure projects.

Interviewer: Generally speaking, do you usually think of yourself as a Democrat, a Republican, an Independent, or what? And how strongly do you associate with that party?

Agent: Independent, and I don't strongly associate with any party.

Interviewer: Who else did you live with?

Agent: I also lived with my younger brother.

Interviewer: Who else did you live with?

Agent: I also lived with my younger sister.

Interviewer: What's the highest degree or grade your mom completed?

Agent: My mom completed a bachelor's degree in education.

Interviewer: Did your mom work for pay for at least a year while you were growing up?

Agent: Yes, my mom worked for pay for several years while I was growing up.

Interviewer: What kind of place did she work for? What kind of business was it? What did they make or do where she worked?

Agent: She worked for a public school. It was an educational institution where they taught children from kindergarten through fifth grade.

Interviewer: What was his job? What kind of work did he do? What were his most important activities or duties?

Agent: He was an engineer. He worked on designing and overseeing the construction of infrastructure projects.

Interviewer: What kind of place did he work for? What kind of business was it? What did they make or do where he worked?

Agent: He worked for an engineering firm that specialized in civil engineering projects, such as building roads and bridges.

Interviewer: What kind of place did he work for? What kind of business was it? What did they make or do where he worked?

Agent: He worked for a construction company that specialized in electrical contracting. They focused on building and infrastructure projects.

Interviewer: We all have hopes about what our future will look like. Imagine yourself a few years from now. Maybe you want your life to be the same in some ways as it is now. Maybe you want it to be different in some ways. What do you hope for?

Agent: I hope to have a fulfilling career, possibly in engineering like my dad, and to have a family of my own.

Interviewer: And that was the last question I wanted to ask today. Thank you so much again for your time. It was really wonderful getting to know you through this interview.

Agent: Thank you for the opportunity to share my experiences. It was great speaking with you too.
